_style: Write standard Haitian Creole (official IPN spelling: ou, m, nou, yo; nasal vowels an/en/on, è/ò with grave accents, no French spellings) in a warm, light, everyday voice, never cheesy and never word-for-word from English. Address the user as “ou” (short form “w” only where it reads naturally after a vowel, e.g. “kounye a w ap…”; prefer the full “ou” in UI labels); for the couple together use “nou de a” / “nou tou de” (“your story” → “istwa nou de a”), and “nou” for the user speaking with the partner. The partner is always “patnè ou” (already gender-neutral) or simply the name placeholder %@; never mennaj/cheri/mari/madanm/nèg/fi, and keep sentences gender-neutral (Creole pronoun “li” is neutral, so “li” is fine for the partner). Determiners and plural “yo” go after the noun (“souvni yo”, “pyebwa a”, “lèt la”) following the usual a/la/an/nan/lan rules; never attach a determiner or any suffix to a placeholder (%@, %lld) and never decline or alter a partner's name: rephrase instead (“%@ voye yon grenn ba ou”, “lèt %@ voye ba ou a”, not “%@ la”). Quotes are curly “ ” (inner ‘ ’), ellipsis is the single character …, apostrophe is straight ' (m', l', n' are written m, l, n without apostrophe in standard spelling: “m ap”, “li la”), no space before ? ! : ; and keep “ · ”, \n, emoji and placeholders exactly. Dates are day-month-year with lowercase months (14 novanm 2026; janvye, fevriye, mas, avril, me, jen, jiyè, out, septanm, oktòb, novanm, desanm), 24-hour or am/pm as the system formats them, numbers with a comma decimal and a space for thousands (1 250,5) when written by hand; nouns do not change after numbers (“%lld jou”, “1 jou”), so the only plural category is ["other"]. Buttons and actions are short bare verbs with no “tanpri” (“Anrejistre”, “Voye lèt la”, “Eseye ankò”); titles, tabs, chips and buttons use sentence case (capital only on the first word), except proper names like Coupley, Premium and IA. Latin script only.
Thinking of You Ping: Ti siy “M ap panse ak ou”
